title: 十个最爱故事与声音的旅行
pdf: https://michael-podcast-1513696684.cos.ap-chengdu.myqcloud.com/vol50/Vol50_晚读讲义_十个最爱故事与声音的旅行_v1.pdf
pdfName: Vol50_晚读讲义_十个最爱故事与声音的旅行_v1.pdf

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome to our fiftieth episode of Michael's Morning Listening! Today we first look back at ten of our favourite stories from the past fifty episodes. Then we follow a tiny traveller — a sound — all the way into your ear. Ready? Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 你好，小小探险家们，欢迎来到 Michael 的早听晚读第五十期！今天，我们先一起回顾过去五十期里最受大家喜欢的十个故事。然后，我们跟随一位小小的旅行者——声音——一路走进你的耳朵。准备好了吗？出发！

blocks.en: Do you remember the flying car? It drove on the road like a car, then spread its wings and flew into the sky! And the bees that learned to play football — they pushed the ball into the goal, one tiny kick at a time. Messi said goodbye to Argentina's home stadium, and the fans sang his name. A robot ran a half marathon beside human runners — slow, steady, and never giving up. A pumpkin grew heavier than a rhino, so big that a whole family could sit inside it!
blocks.title: 十个最爱故事
blocks.cn: 还记得会飞的汽车吗？它在路上像汽车一样开，然后展开翅膀飞上天空！还有学会踢足球的蜜蜂——它们一脚一脚地把球推进球门。梅西告别了阿根廷的主场，球迷们齐声高唱他的名字。一个机器人和人类跑者一起跑完了半程马拉松——慢慢的、稳稳的、从不放弃。一个南瓜长得比犀牛还重，大到一家人都能坐进去！

blocks.en: A cat became the boss of a library, sleeping on the books and greeting every reader at the door. A hundred-year-old grandpa jumped out of a plane with a parachute — age is only a number! A penguin proposed with a pebble, offering the smoothest stone he could find to the one he loved. The mantis shrimp sees colours we cannot imagine, with eyes that move on their own. And Lucy, the little girl who grew a sunflower taller than a bus — small hands, huge surprise!
blocks.title: 十个最爱故事
blocks.cn: 一只猫当上了图书馆的馆长，睡在书上，在门口迎接每一位读者。一位一百岁的爷爷带着降落伞跳出飞机——年龄只是一个数字！一只企鹅用一颗鹅卵石求婚，把它能找到的最光滑的石头送给心爱的那一位。皮皮虾能看到我们无法想象的颜色，它的眼睛还能自己转动。还有露西，那个种出比巴士还高的向日葵的小姑娘——小小的双手，大大的惊喜！

blocks.en: Every sound begins with a shake. Hit a drum, and its skin shakes back and forth. That shake is called a vibration, and it pushes the air into a wave. Our approach is simple: follow that wave, step by step, all the way into your ear. First, your outer ear catches the wave and funnels it down the ear canal to a thin piece of tissue called the eardrum. The wave makes the eardrum shake!
blocks.title: 声音的旅行
blocks.cn: 每一个声音都从一次震动开始。敲一下鼓，鼓面就会来回震动。这种震动叫做 vibration（振动），它把空气推成一波波的声波。我们的方法很简单：一步一步地跟随这波声波，一路走进你的耳朵。首先，你的外耳接住声波，把它送进耳道，传到一层薄薄的组织——耳膜。声波让耳膜也震动起来！

blocks.en: Next, the shake reaches three tiny bones — the hammer, the anvil and the stirrup. They are the smallest bones in your body, and they conduct the shake onward, making it stronger. Then comes the most amazing aspect: a snail-shaped room full of fluid, called the cochlea. Inside, thousands of tiny hair cells bend like grass in the wind, and their bending turns the shake into electrical signals. Those signals race along the auditory nerve to your brain, and your brain reads them as a sparrow's song, a friend's laugh, or music. Sound moves as a pulse through the air at about 343 metres every second.
blocks.title: 声音的旅行
blocks.cn: 接着，震动传到三块小小的骨头——锤骨、砧骨和镫骨。它们是你身体里最小的骨头，能把震动继续传下去，还让它变得更强。然后是最神奇的一幕：一个像蜗牛壳一样的、装满液体的房间，叫做 cochlea（耳蜗）。里面，成千上万根细小的毛细胞像风中的小草一样弯曲，它们的弯曲把震动变成了电信号。这些信号沿着听觉神经飞奔到你的大脑，大脑把它们解读成麻雀的歌声、朋友的笑声，或者音乐。声音以脉冲的形式在空气中传播，每秒大约 343 米。

blocks.en: And here is a fun fact: sound needs something to travel through. In empty space, with no air at all, there is no sound — that is why space is silent! So remember the journey: shake, wave, eardrum, bones, cochlea, brain — all in less than a blink!
blocks.title: 声音的旅行
blocks.cn: 还有一个有趣的事实：声音需要东西来传播。在空无一物的太空里，完全没有空气，也就没有声音——所以太空是安静的！记住这趟旅程吧：震动、声波、耳膜、骨头、耳蜗、大脑——全部不到眨一下眼的时间！

blocks.en: Today's idiom is "your guess is as good as mine." It means "I don't know either!" For example: if you ask me how many songs a sparrow can sing, your guess is as good as mine! Try it: when a friend asks you something nobody knows, just smile and say: your guess is as good as mine!
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是“your guess is as good as mine”（你的猜测和我的一样好）。它的意思是“我也不知道！”举个例子：如果你问我一只麻雀会唱多少首歌，your guess is as good as mine！试试用它：当朋友问你一个谁也不知道答案的问题时，就微笑着说：your guess is as good as mine！

blocks.en: Now it is your turn! One: which of our ten favourite stories do you like best, and why? Two: sound cannot travel in empty space — can you think of another place where sound travels, like water or a wall? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 现在轮到你们啦！第一：在我们回顾的十个最爱的故事里，你最喜欢哪一个，为什么？第二：声音不能在空无一物的太空里传播——你能想到声音还能在什么地方传播吗，比如水里或者墙里？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That is all for today, young explorers — and thank you for fifty wonderful episodes! Keep your ears open, keep asking questions, and we will meet tomorrow morning. Goodbye, and have a wonderful day!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们——谢谢你们陪伴我们度过五十期精彩的节目！竖起耳朵，继续提问，我们明天早上再见。再见，祝你度过美好的一天！

quiz.title: B. 单项选择（Single Choice）
questions:
Which story is about a robot?
A. A robot that ran a half marathon
B. A robot that grew a sunflower
C. A robot that sang songs
D. A robot that played football

What makes the eardrum shake?
A. Light
B. A sound wave
C. Water
D. A magnet

What do the hair cells in the cochlea do?
A. They turn shakes into electrical signals
B. They make sounds louder
C. They stop sounds
D. They clean the ear

What does "your guess is as good as mine" mean?
A. Your guess is better than mine
B. I don't know either
C. You must guess again
D. I know the answer

children.text: Inside, thousands of tiny hair cells bend like grass in the wind, and their bending turns the shake into electrical signals.
：thousands of（成千上万的）+ tiny hair cells（细小的毛细胞，复数），意思是“成千上万根细小的毛细胞”。说“成千上万个……”时，英语就用 thousands of + 复数名词。
bend like grass in the wind
：bend（弯曲）+ like（像）+ grass in the wind（风中的小草），意思是“像风中的小草一样弯曲”。like 后面直接跟拿来打比方的名词。
their bending turns the shake into electrical signals
their bending（它们的弯曲）是动名词短语作主语
——bend（弯曲）+ ing 变成 bending（弯曲这件事），前面加 their（它们的），整个短语当主语；
turn A into B（把 A 变成 B）
：turn（变成）+ the shake（震动）+ into（成）+ electrical signals（电信号），意思是“把震动变成电信号”。
成千上万（thousands of）→ 像小草一样弯（bend like grass）→ 弯曲把震动变成信号（bending turns … into …）
。一句话里藏着数量表达、明喻和动名词主语三个机关。
"A robot ran a half marathon beside human runners."
"your outer ear catches the wave ... The wave makes the eardrum shake!"
"their bending turns the shake into electrical signals."
D. Your own translations — there is no key for this part. Read your Chinese aloud and check that it sounds natural.
